title: 5.2.13 Pinball Scene
description: Build a pinball-style scene: static obstacles, a bouncy ball, gravity, and a reset key. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Turn on gravity
steps.instructions: Set world.gravity.y to a non-zero value so the ball falls.
hints: Search the moSHion docs drawer for world.gravity.

steps.title: Build at least three static obstacles
steps.instructions: Create at least three static sprites: bumpers, ramps, or walls the ball can bounce off of. Give each one a shape, position, and color.
hints: Check the Sprite section of the moSHion docs drawer for the 'static' argument.

steps.title: Add a bouncy ball
steps.instructions: Create the ball as a dynamic sprite and set its bounciness above 0.8 so it feels lively, not sticky.
hints: Look up sprite properties in the moSHion docs drawer.

steps.title: Add a reset key
steps.instructions: When a key is pressed, move the ball back to a starting position near the top of the canvas.
hints: Search the moSHion docs drawer for kb.presses.

requirements.title: Turn on gravity
requirements.description: world.gravity.y is set to a non-zero value. Help: 5.2.2 (Gravity)

requirements.title: Add at least three static obstacles
requirements.description: At least three 'static' sprites exist in the scene. Help: 5.2.6 (Bounciness and Friction)

requirements.title: Make the ball genuinely bouncy
requirements.description: The ball's bounciness is set above 0.8. Help: 5.2.6 (Bounciness and Friction)

requirements.title: Add a reset key
requirements.description: Pressing a key repositions the ball (sets its x and/or y) so a lost ball can be brought back to the top. Help: 5.2.6 (Bounciness and Friction)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote a moSHion sketch (p5-style JavaScript with a physics world) for the lab "5.2.13 Pinball Scene". The task they were given: Build a pinball-style scene: static obstacles, a bouncy ball, gravity, and a reset key. You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do when the sketch runs. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
